name: Copper Clad Laminates & PCB Base Materials
scope: The global CCL, glass cloth and copper foil squeeze driven by AI servers, and India's first ECMS-backed laminate plants at Ratnaveer, Kaynes, Syrma and (newly tracked) Amber; Wipro's plant is unlisted.

summary.one_line: Laminate prices kept rising into September: Nan Ya raised CCL prices 20% and Kingboard up to 20%. The squeeze is now visible in Indian results, with Amber's PCB margin down to ~12% from 16%. India's first CCL line, at Ratnaveer, opens order booking on 31 Oct. Ratnaveer is the only real laminate play, and its stock is near its 52-week high.
key_points: Global prices are still rising. Nan Ya raised CCL and base-material prices 20% from 1 Sep 2026 (S17). Kingboard raised FR-4 by 10% and thin prepreg by 20% on 28 Aug, citing glass cloth and copper foil costs (S18). Standard 7628 glass cloth reached $1.47/m in Aug 2026, up 140% in a year (S1).

Korean CCL import prices hit $20,728/t in Mar 2026, up 74.5% YoY (S16). Premium-grade lead times are 20-30 weeks and global CCL utilisation is 92-95% (S2). Big new supply arrives only in 2027-28: Doosan's Thailand CCL plant targets mass production in H2 2028 (S2, S16).

India depends on imported CCL: 100% per Wipro's announcement (S14), and over 90% per Ratnaveer, which sizes the domestic CCL market at more than Rs 5,000 cr (S7). Ind-Ra notes the imports come from China, and that a 30% anti-dumping duty on bare PCBs is already driving local PCB output (S20).

Under ECMS, laminate, copper foil and prepreg get a 25% capex incentive and no turnover-linked incentive (S3). Cumulative approvals stand at Rs 69,548 cr after the 17 Aug 2026 tranche, which included Rs 1,033 cr more for Wipro's CCL plant (S15). We found no new tranche between 17 Aug and 7 Oct.

Ratnaveer's CCL project is ~60% complete. Order booking starts 31 Oct, trial production is due in the second week of Dec 2026, and inauguration around mid-Jan 2027 (S6). It is funded partly by a Rs 329.99 cr rights issue at Rs 264 (S5). ICICI Direct's estimates still exclude CCL. Management's FY31 case is Rs 750+ cr CCL revenue at a 20% EBITDA margin (S7).

New this week: Amber Enterprises says sharp CCL price rises have cut its PCB margin to ~12% from a normal 16%, and it expects its first CCL plant by FY29-30 (S19). Kaynes and Syrma are still PCB-first stories; laminates will not affect their earnings before FY28 (S11, S13).

Valuations as of 6 Oct 2026: Ratnaveer trades at 44.5x P/E, 5.8% below its 52-week high, against Rs 197 at ICICI Direct's 27 Jul note. Syrma is at 81.6x, 6.7% off its high. Kaynes is at 66x, 55.9% below its 52-week high (S8, S9, S10, S7).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Ratnaveer: line 1 starts while CCL prices are high and still rising (S6, S17, S18). Management targets Rs 750+ cr CCL revenue, Rs 150 cr EBITDA and a 29% ROI at scale by FY31 (S7).
Indian PCB makers (Kaynes, Amber, Syrma) would gain a local laminate source and save on freight and duties. Amber and Kaynes both plan in-house CCL (S4, S19).

Epoxy suppliers to electrical and electronics markets (Atul, Grasim's Advanced Materials) could gain a new local customer base if CCL lines scale (S23, S24). This is our inference; neither company has disclosed CCL-specific supply.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Indian PCB and EMS makers that buy imported laminates. Amber's PCB margin fell to ~12% from 16% (S19). At Kaynes, component prices are up 30-35% and lead times have stretched to 6-8 months (S13).

New Indian CCL lines will still import glass cloth and copper foil, the inputs CCL makers blame for their hikes; glass cloth alone is up 140% in a year (S1, S18). Ratnaveer's machinery comes from China (S6).
Ratnaveer has re-rated ahead of first output: Rs 339 on 6 Oct vs Rs 197 on 27 Jul and the Rs 264 rights price (S8, S7, S5). Customers are unnamed and contracts are unsigned (S6).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Ratnaveer order bookings from 31 Oct 2026, trial production in the second week of Dec, and inauguration around mid-Jan 2027 (S6).
Kaynes and Amber PCB plant start-ups: Kaynes' commercialisation is due from Q3 FY27, and Amber's Hosur plant within FY27 (S13, S19).
Whether CCL prices keep rising after the Nan Ya and Kingboard hikes, and the 7628 glass cloth forecast of $1.75-2.19/m for Q4 2026 (S1, S17, S18).

sections.title: What CCL is and why it is tight

subsections.title: CCL and prepreg in the PCB value chain

blocks.text: A copper clad laminate (CCL) is the base sheet of a PCB: woven glass fibre impregnated with resin (usually epoxy) and covered with copper foil on one or both sides. Prepreg is the resin-impregnated glass layer that insulates and bonds the layers of a multi-layer PCB (S4). The three inputs are glass cloth, copper foil and resin. Kingboard and Nan Ya both cite all three as the cost drivers behind their 2026 price hikes (S17, S18).
AI servers need low-loss laminates (e.g. Megtron 7 class), NE-glass thin cores and very-low-profile copper foil. AtlasPCB describes all of these as 'allocation-only' (S2).

blocks.text: New supply takes time. Glass weaving looms have 18-24 month lead times, and AtlasPCB expects new glass cloth capacity from mid-to-late 2027 (S1). A new CCL line takes 18-24 months to build (S2). Doosan's new CCL plant in Thailand targets mass production in H2 2028, and order books at CCL equipment vendors stretch to 2028 (S16).
The price data comes from trade press (AtlasPCB, SMM, EMSNow) and supplier notices. None of it is an audited index. Supplier hikes are list-price announcements, and realised prices may differ.

sections.title: Import dependence, ECMS and Indian laminate capex

blocks.text: Wipro's 2025 announcement says India imports 100% of its CCL (S14). Ratnaveer puts the share at over 90% of a domestic market worth more than Rs 5,000 cr, and projects the market could reach Rs 29,880 cr by 2031 (company estimate, S7). Ind-Ra notes that India's CCL comes mainly from China. A 30% anti-dumping duty on bare PCBs, in force from March 2024 for five years, lifted domestic PCB plant utilisation to 70-90%. Ind-Ra concluded that without local CCL, value addition will stay limited (S20).

subsections.title: Ratnaveer: a steel company adding a laminate business

blocks.text: Ratnaveer makes stainless steel sheets, washers, solar roofing hooks, pipes and tubes. In FY26, finishing-line sheets made up ~53% of revenue (S7). In Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.9% YoY to Rs 315 cr at a 10.2% EBITDA margin (S7). Line 1 machinery was ordered and inspected, and has left China (S6, S7). The company reports soft confirmations from customers for long-term, possibly exclusive contracts, but has named no customers (S6).

blocks.text: At scale, CCL would be about 30% of group revenue but a larger share of EBITDA. That case rests on management targets and on CCL prices that are currently far above 2025 levels (S1, S7).

blocks.text: Sources disagree on how much PCB prices have risen. On the Q1 FY27 call, Kaynes management was reported as saying PCB prices had roughly tripled (S12). ICICI Direct's call notes record PCB prices up 10-12% and component prices up 30-35% (S13). Amber says PCB price pass-through is ongoing, and margins should return to 15-16% from Q3 FY27 if CCL prices do not rise further (S19). The Nan Ya and Kingboard hikes in late August test that assumption (S17, S18).

subsections.title: Can Indian plants make AI-server grades?

blocks.text: No Indian company has disclosed qualification for ultra-low-loss grades, a segment led by Japanese, Taiwanese and US suppliers (S2). Ratnaveer has not disclosed which grades it will make, and its equipment comes from China (S6). Its management targets PCB, EV, defence and semiconductor tailwinds rather than AI servers specifically (S7). BSE-listed Fine-Line Circuits already builds RF/microwave PCBs on imported PTFE and polyimide substrates (S25).

Our reading: the first Indian lines will most likely make standard FR-4 for consumer, auto and industrial PCBs, with glass cloth and copper foil imported at first. No source confirms domestic supply of PCB-grade glass cloth or copper foil. Ram Ratna Wires' 2023 plan for PCB laminates and copper foil has had no follow-up disclosure that we could find (S22).

subsections.title: Broker and rating-agency coverage of the laminate angle

items: ICICI Direct (27 Jul 2026) covers Ratnaveer, which corrects last week's edition: we had found no broker coverage. The note calls CCL the next growth leg but leaves CCL out of its FY27-28 estimates until execution is clearer. It forecasts FY28E revenue of Rs 1,475 cr and PAT of Rs 84 cr from steel alone (S7).
ICICI Direct (17 Aug 2026) on Amber is the only broker note we found that quantifies the CCL cost hit to an Indian PCB maker: PCB margin of ~12% against a normal 16% (S19).
ICICI Direct (11 Aug 2026) on Kaynes puts the focus on working capital: receivables are Rs 1,925 cr. It expects OSAT and PCB commercialisation from Q3 FY27 (S13).

Motilal Oswal (24 Feb 2026) names CCL self-sufficiency for Kaynes and a PCB plant for Syrma targeting INR 25b in revenue (S4). ICICI Direct (13 May 2026) expects Syrma's PCB and CCL business to support margins from FY28 (S11).
Ind-Ra (Jun 2025) treats local CCL as the missing link for margin expansion in Indian PCB (S20).

Market cap Rs 27,482 cr on 1 Jul 2026 (Trade Brains)

blocks.text: Sources: S8, S9, S10, S7, S13, S21, S5. Ratnaveer is up ~72% since 27 Jul and trades ~28% above its rights price. That puts much of the CCL optionality in the price before first output, even though the broker estimates exclude CCL (S7, S8). Kaynes' de-rating comes from working capital and core-EMS concerns rather than laminates (S13).

items: Commissioning slippage: Ratnaveer guided for commercial production in November 2026 (S7) but now plans trial production in December and inauguration in mid-January 2027 (S6). Kaynes cited a minor slippage from the West Asia conflict and now targets Q3 FY27 (S12, S13).
Raw materials: glass cloth is up 140% (S1), and suppliers blame glass cloth and copper foil for CCL hikes (S18). Indian lines will import these inputs and so face the same cost inflation.
Price cycle: new capacity in 2027-28, including Doosan in Thailand in H2 2028, could reverse prices just as Indian lines ramp up (S2, S16).
Customer qualification: Ratnaveer has disclosed only soft confirmations and no named customers (S6).

Funding and balance sheet: Ratnaveer raised Rs 329.99 cr through its rights issue as part of a Rs 650 cr funding package (S5). Its debt is expected to rise from Rs 335 cr in FY26 to Rs 475 cr by FY28E (S7). Amber's net debt rose to ~Rs 1,225 cr in Jun 2026 from ~Rs 510 cr in Mar 2026 (S19).

companies.name: Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Ltd
companies.role: Stainless steel products maker building an ECMS-approved CCL plant in Vadodara: Rs 338 cr phase 1, Rs 472.34 cr total (S7).
companies.impact: Order booking begins 31 Oct and trial production is due in Dec 2026 (S6). Management targets Rs 750+ cr CCL revenue at a 20% EBITDA margin by FY31 (S7). The stock trades at 44.5x P/E near its 52-week high (S8).

companies.name: Kaynes Technology India Ltd
companies.role: EMS company whose subsidiary Kaynes Circuits holds an INR 32.8b ECMS grant approval for multi-layer and HDI PCBs, camera modules and CCL (S4).
companies.impact: PCB and OSAT commercialisation is due from Q3 FY27, and one global customer has asked for the entire PCB capacity (S13). CCL mainly lowers its own PCB costs. The stock is 55.9% below its 52-week high on working-capital concerns (S9, S13).

companies.name: Syrma SGS Technology Ltd
companies.role: EMS company with ECMS approvals for CCL, HDI and flex PCB, and a planned PCB plant targeting INR 25b of revenue (S4, S11).
companies.impact: Laminates will not affect earnings before FY28. CCL capex of ~Rs 800 cr is planned for FY28-30 (S11). The stock trades at 81.6x P/E (S10).

companies.name: Amber Enterprises India Ltd
companies.role: AC and EMS maker investing ~Rs 4,300 cr in bare PCBs under ECMS (Hosur, Jewar HDI, Shogini). It plans its first CCL plant by FY29-30 (S19).
companies.impact: Its PCB margin fell to ~12% from a normal 16% on CCL price rises. Recovery from Q3 FY27 assumes no further CCL hikes (S19), but Nan Ya and Kingboard raised prices again in late August (S17, S18).

companies.name: Ram Ratna Wires Ltd
companies.role: Copper winding wire maker. Its board approved a Bhiwadi facility for PCBs, PCB laminates and copper foil in Mar 2023, at Rs 200 cr over five years (S22).
companies.impact: This is a stated laminate and copper foil ambition with no further disclosure on laminates that we found. Treat it as an option, not a project.

companies.name: Fine-Line Circuits Ltd
companies.role: Microcap PCB maker in SEEPZ Mumbai. PCBs are 100% of its revenue, including RF boards on PTFE and polyimide substrates (S25).
companies.impact: A laminate buyer: exposed to imported CCL cost inflation (S17, S18) and a likely beneficiary of local supply over time. No laminate plans have been disclosed.

companies.name: Cyient DLM Ltd
companies.role: Design-led EMS and PCB assembly for high-reliability sectors (S21).
companies.impact: Adjacent only. Higher PCB and component costs flow through its bill of materials (S13, S21). It has no disclosed laminate project.

companies.name: Atul Ltd
companies.role: Makes Lapox epoxy resins, curing agents and diluents for markets including electrical and electronics (S23).
companies.impact: A potential local resin supplier to CCL lines. CCL-specific supply has not been disclosed, so this is adjacent only.

companies.name: Grasim Industries Ltd
companies.role: Its Aditya Birla Advanced Materials epoxy business serves electrical and electronics among other sectors (S24).
companies.impact: Adjacent large-cap resin supplier. Laminate demand would be a small share of its business, and no CCL-specific supply has been disclosed.

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W40 edition, researched on 7 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. Market data comes from screener.in as of 6 Oct 2026 (numbers.json). New this week: supplier price notices (Nan Ya, Kingboard), Korean CCL import prices, ICICI Direct Q1 FY27 notes on Ratnaveer, Kaynes and Amber (read from the PDFs), and an Ind-Ra view on CCL dependence. We also widened the universe to Amber (PCB, with CCL planned) and to adjacent names: Ram Ratna Wires, Fine-Line Circuits, Cyient DLM, Atul and Grasim. Dropped from last week: Trade Brains' Rs 338 cr / 15.84 lakh sheet figures and Business Today's FY28 Ratnaveer guidance, now replaced by the ICICI Direct-reported management case; Multibagg's Kaynes PAT figure; and secondary Kaynes sell-off coverage. Corrections: last week said Ratnaveer had no broker coverage, but ICICI Direct published a note on 27 Jul 2026. India's CCL import share is now shown as 90-100% because sources differ. No new ECMS tranche was found between 17 Aug and 7 Oct 2026. PIB and BSE filing pages returned 403, so the policy figures rely on secondary reports. Not included: Trade Brains' claim that SRF produces CCL, which we could not confirm; Hindalco's copper foil plans, which are battery-focused and early-stage with no PCB-grade disclosure found; and a reported bulk deal in Ratnaveer seen only in a search snippet. Coverage spans large cap (Grasim), mid cap (Kaynes, Syrma, Amber, Atul), small cap (Ratnaveer, Ram Ratna, Cyient DLM) and microcap (Fine-Line). Ratnaveer is still the only listed company with a standalone laminate plant near commissioning. The 'other' bucket names are adjacent, not laminate makers. No ratings or price targets are given; broker targets were deliberately omitted.
